name: mild_day_planned_window_gate_refuses_pauses_1211
description: Mild day (forecast high 72 / low 52: the real classifier recommends windows, so the 10:00-17:00 planned window period is active), whole-house fan configured, but the house is cool (indoor 69, below the 70 F floor) so the nat-vent entry gate refuses. A window opens at 12:00 inside the period: the handler runs the gate and pauses right there, never a silent no-op (Issue #1211 A3 / owner decision O8b).
source: Issue #1211 pending scenario (promote only with owner review)
notes: Issue #1211 (A3, single behaviour): the classification states no windows_recommended; the harness fills it from classify_day (high 72 / low 52 on a mild day with a 70 F floor -> True, times 10:00/17:00), so the planned period is genuinely active at 12:00. The gate refuses on temperature (indoor 69 < floor 70) with a working fan configured, so the only thing that can make the HVAC pause is the handler itself.

Revert-check: restoring the planned-window early return in handle_door_window_open() makes the 12:00 assertion fail (the handler returns silently; no pause). Reverting the classifier alone does not change this scenario (flag True either way), so it pins A3 only. The classifier's cold-forecast answer (mild 65/49 -> not recommended) is pinned by tests/test_classifier.py and the briefing corpus: once A3 landed, no scenario decision depends on the flag except the lazy reconcile, which a scenario cannot reach without an unhandled open window.

Three-exercise protocol: (a) effectiveness: see the revert-check; (b) docs: docs/08 C2/C5 rows say the open window pauses when the gate refuses; (c) occupant: if it regressed the HVAC would keep heating into an open window until the next coordinator refresh.

Issue #1200 (2026-11-01, pending owner approval): a whole-house fan install requires at least one door/window sensor; a sensorless WHF is unsupported. The scenario now configures binary_sensor.living_room_window so it runs in a supported configuration. In the engine-only harness the WHF safety logic already saw one sensor (the harness's open-sensor tracker), so this edit only makes the config say what the run already modelled: assertions and the full event log are unchanged.

events.note: Late morning: indoor 69F (below the 70F floor), outdoor 60F
Mild day, forecast high 72 / low 52: the real classifier decides (windows recommended, period 10:00-17:00)
Window opens at 12:00 inside the planned period; nat-vent gate refuses (indoor below the floor) -> pause

assertions.reason: Window left open, nat-vent refused (indoor 69 < floor 70): the handler pauses (Issue #1211).

verdict.summary: A window opened inside the planned period on a mild day, with the nat-vent gate refusing (house below the floor), pauses the HVAC at once; no silent no-op
